survey: A chunky blue calculator floats at an angle against a yellow pi-pattern background. Its body is a thick rounded slab tilted back and rotated, so the bottom-left edge is nearest the viewer and the top recedes; the thickness shows along the left and bottom sides. On the face, from top to bottom, are a red solar strip, a grey display window, and a 4x4 keypad: cream number keys 7-9, 4-6, 1-3 and 0/./= in three columns, with a column of cyan operator keys (÷ × − +) on the right. The display and solar strip are drawn at a slight slant, roughly in line with the tilted face. The keys are thick rounded caps that stick out from the face.

errors.where: Keypad (all 16 keys) on the calculator face
errors.what: The body is tilted back and turned, so its face recedes toward the top. Yet every key is drawn almost front-on at the same size and spacing: the far 7-8-9-÷ row is as large and wide as the near 0-.-=-+ row. The keys do not shrink or flatten with the face, and their visible side walls all face the same way. The key grid reads as a flat sticker laid over the tilted body, not as keys set into its surface. This is the same mistake as in the first reference example.

errors.where: Rows and columns of the keypad compared with the body edges and the display
errors.what: The key rows slope down to the right more steeply than the top edge of the body and the bottom edge of the display. The key columns also lean differently from the left and right sides of the body. So the grid does not sit on lines parallel to the face's edges, and the keypad looks rotated against the body.

fix: Draw the keypad in true perspective on the tilted face of the calculator. Rows farther from the viewer (7 8 9 ÷) should be smaller, flatter and closer together than the near rows (0 . = +). Each key should be foreshortened like the face, and its sides should show at the same angle as the body's thickness. Key rows must run parallel to the top and bottom edges of the body and the display, and key columns parallel to its left and right sides, all toward the same vanishing points as the body.
